children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were correcting themselves Wednesday morning, one day after rallying to their highest prices of the year.

Crude oil prices were in decline despite new attacks between the U.S. and Iran. U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of crude oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz Monday, the largest one-day amount since the start of the war.
Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil also were in negative territory.

The northern half of Alberta will see rain Wednesday, while the southern half will be sunny. However, there will be chances of rain and thunderstorms in the late hours across the province. Saskatchewan and southern Manitoba will be sunny with temperatures in the mid- to high-20 degrees Celsius.
The Canadian dollar was down less than one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared with Tuesday's close. The Bank of Canada announced Wednesday it was keeping its key interest rate at 2.25%.
Nearly 23,800 contracts were traded. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton as of 9:41 a.m. ET:
